rationale: All seven of my round-3 asks are addressed at a593792a (F3r3.4's premise was correctly refuted in part: a no-lineage bug is already refused by EvaluateReadiness today). The four rulings hold up under attack except at two seams, both fixable in the text. (1) The reattest-audited read-back is not bound to the identity it vouches: the audit keys (`mindspec_landed_reattest_{actor,at,op,corroboration,prior_merge_sha,prior_second_parent,scanned_branch}`) carry no merge SHA or second parent, the binding SHA keys are shared with the executor's merge-time write, and both writers go through `bead.MergeMetadata` (read-merge-write), so audit keys survive any later rewrite of the SHA keys. A merge-time binding on a bead that was reattested once earlier therefore reads as 'reattest-audited', contradicting R4.2's own rule, and the cheap forge is editing two SHA keys on an already-audited bead. I wrote all six keys with `bd update --metadata` on a scratch bd 1.1.0 and read them back. What bounds it today is only inspection; the spec can bound it structurally by binding the audit to the vouched identity and by re-running reattest's two structural refusals (pure git/panel reads) on the automatic read. (2) R1.1 (c) defines 'mapped' as a `## Bead N` section OR a `work_chunks` id N, but `evaluateMF1` requires BOTH and `extractBeadSectionRaw` maps N to the Nth `## Bead` heading by count, not by its number. Under OR a row mapped by only one of the two is a member that MF-1 then refuses — the selected-then-refused class Ruling 2 exists to remove. Everything else is MINOR.
concrete_changes_required: R4.2 read-back: bind the audit to the identity it vouched. Require the reattest write to record the vouched pair under audit keys (e.g. `mindspec_landed_reattest_merge_sha` and `mindspec_landed_reattest_second_parent`, or parse them from the existing `corroboration` string), and define the automatic read-back of a fallback candidate as: binding SHA keys == audit SHA keys == the scan-derived candidate, AND `scanned_branch` == this spec branch. Today the executor's merge-time write (`mergeBindingFn = bead.MergeMetadata`) and reattest's write (`reattestBindingFn = bead.MergeMetadata`) both merge into the same metadata map, so a later executor rewrite of the two SHA keys leaves an earlier audit intact and the spec's 'a merge-time binding never confirms a fallback candidate' is false for any bead that was ever reattested. Add an AC-11 leg: prior reattest audit, then a merge-time rewrite of the SHA keys to a fallback candidate → MF-3 FAILS with the reattest recovery.

R4.2 read-back: bound the forge structurally. On every automatic read that would accept a fallback candidate through an audited binding, re-run reattest's refusals (i) exactly one admitted fallback candidate and (ii) no registered `reviewed_head_sha` outside the tip's history. Both are git/panel reads, not metadata, so a forged or stale audit can never bypass the refusals this round introduced; the audit then attests only the operator's vouch. State the residual that remains after this (an agent can still write the audit, but only for a candidate that would pass reattest anyway). Extend AC-11 (ix) from 'binding without audit keys' to 'binding WITH a complete forged audit' in the O3 round-2 shape: MF-3 still FAILS because (ii) fails on B.

R1.1 (c): define 'mapped' as MF-1's exact precondition, through one shared helper (e.g. `readiness.PlanMapsBead(planContent, n) bool`) used by both selection and `evaluateMF1`: the plan has at least N `## Bead ` sections (positional — `extractBeadSectionRaw` selects the Nth heading by count and ignores the heading's own number) AND `work_chunks` carries an entry with id N. Replace 'or' with 'and', state the positional semantics, and reword N4's message to what is true (`plan.md declares <K> beads and no work_chunks id <N>`). Add AC-1 rows: `<E>.K+1` with a work_chunks id K+1 but no section → N4 (not a member); a plan with K sections whose headings are non-contiguous → membership by count, pinned.

R1.2 N2b: the title tag contradicts E, so the reparent is only correct when the bead belongs to S. Split by whether E2's spec number equals S's number (a duplicate-epic case, reparent is right) or differs (the title names another spec; the bead may have been minted under E by mistake). For the differing case make `bd show <id> --json` the first line and state the reparent as the second line, conditional on the bead belonging to S. Pin both in AC-2.

R1.1: state where `plan.md` is read from for the membership mapping and what `--emit-only` does when the invoking checkout lacks it. `workspace.SpecDir(root, S)/plan.md` is the invoking checkout's file; during implementation the plan lives on the spec branch, so an orchestrator running `mindspec next --spec S --emit-only` from a main checkout (which works today — no gate runs on that path) would now refuse with 'could not read plan.md'. Either read the plan from `spec/<S>` via git when the checkout lacks it, or pin the refusal and name the recovery (run from the spec worktree). Add an AC-1 leg.

findings.title: The reattest audit is not bound to the merge it vouched, so a merge-time binding with a stale audit — or a two-key edit — reads as reattest-audited
findings.detail: R4.2 accepts a fallback candidate on later automatic reads iff the binding names the merge SHA and second parent AND it 'carries a reattest audit record whose scanned branch is this spec branch'. The audit keys written by `ReattestLandedMerge` (internal/lifecycle/reattest.go) are actor, at, op, corroboration, prior_merge_sha, prior_second_parent and scanned_branch — none is the vouched merge SHA or second parent; those live only in the two binding keys that the executor's merge-time write also owns. Both writers default to `bead.MergeMetadata`, a read-merge-write, so a later binding rewrite preserves the old audit keys. Accident: bead X reattested once on the primary path (audit written), later re-merged by `complete` (executor rewrites the SHA keys), then the #239 topology — the merge-time binding now names a fallback candidate and carries an audit with the right scanned_branch, and the automatic read accepts it; AC-11 (xi) is green only for a bead with no prior audit. Forge: on any already-audited bead the attacker edits two SHA keys; on any bead, all six keys are one `bd update --metadata` away (verified on scratch bd 1.1.0: written and read back intact). What bounds it today: the candidate must be a real reachable two-parent merge with an admitted subject naming bead/X (git-history threat boundary) and the spec's 'detectable by inspection'. What can bound it cheaply: bind the audit to the vouched pair, and re-run reattest's refusals (i) and (ii) on the automatic read — both are git/panel reads a metadata forge cannot satisfy.

findings.title: R1.1 (c)'s 'mapped' (section OR work_chunks id) is wider than MF-1's precondition, and sections are positional
findings.detail: `evaluateMF1` fails when the Nth section is absent (`sectionFound == false`) AND separately when `work_chunks` has no entry with id N (`chunk == nil`); a PASS needs both. `extractBeadSectionRaw(content, n)` counts `## Bead ` headings and captures the Nth by COUNT — the heading's own number is never parsed. So under the spec's OR, a `<E>.7` row whose plan has a `work_chunks` id 7 but only six sections, or seven sections but no chunk 7, is a member that is selected and then refused NOT-READY on MF-1 — the outcome Ruling 2 was meant to remove. Under AND nothing is wrongly hidden: a row that AND excludes is one MF-1 would refuse. The N4 sentence 'no Bead <N>' should say what the mapping tests. One shared helper keeps selection and MF-1 from drifting.

findings.title: N2b's reparent can misattribute when the title names a different spec
findings.detail: N2b fires when a plan-form row with no parent resolves to E2 through the title number. If E2's number equals S's number (duplicate epics for one spec), reparenting to E is right. If the title names another spec's number (`[130] …` under `<E129>.N`), the row may have been minted under E by mistake, and `bd update <id> --parent <E>` would attach the other spec's work to S. The Spec-127 principle is 'never reparent over something the agent did not name'; the title tag is such a thing.

findings.title: Membership now needs plan.md in the invoking checkout; `--emit-only` from a main checkout would newly refuse
findings.detail: R1.1 reads `plan.md` once per scoped call and refuses the whole command when it is unreadable. `workspace.SpecDir(root, S)` resolves against the invoking checkout, and during implementation the plan exists on the spec branch, not necessarily on main. Today `next --spec S --emit-only` from main runs no gate and works (bd-only selection); under R1.1 it refuses. State the source of plan.md (checkout file, or `git show spec/<S>:…` fallback) and pin the emit-only behaviour.

findings.title: Attacks that did not land, and one unverified premise
findings.detail: Mapped N still non-claimable for a legitimate reason: a mapped section that is only the scaffold placeholder, or MF-2/3/4 failures — those are what the gate is for, and selecting-then-refusing is correct there. N4 positional → GateReadiness → MF-1 refusal → `--allow-not-ready=MF-1 --evidence` claims it, then R1.8 (a) holds (plan form) and dispatch goes to T: consistent. A sub-epic child `<E>.N` of type epic appears in `bd ready` (verified) and is stripped by the epic rule. N4 beads that block a plan bead leave the member set empty with the `none selectable` line and exit 0: acceptable. Per-record digests: growth/shrink semantics are right; digests of short canonical records are trivially forgeable but the marker is unauthenticated by design. Unverified: on scratch bd 1.1.0, `bd dep add <X> <E2>` (X under E, E2 another epic) left `bd show X` showing only the parent-child edge, so I could not produce the N2c / AC-1 row X shape on a real bd in this probe (bd's output was suppressed, so the add may have been rejected); the fake-bd test can still model it, but the plan should confirm bd can create a blocks edge onto an epic before relying on N2c being reachable. No worktree was created; the scratch db under r4/F3 is removed.
